note: What a person wants now, the goal they carry for the future, and what they do for pleasure. Original writing for Pathfinder GM (2026-09-25); the goals follow the shape of Dwarf Fortress's life goals, not its words. Each row may declare: classes (the work classes it fits; absent = any), requires (at least one of these tags must already be rolled), excludes (none of these tags may be rolled). Tags are the occupation tags, the occupation class, and the personality pole ids. minor: the tag a child's work carries; adult-only rows exclude it.

wants.text: to pay off what they owe a moneylender before the next quarter-day
to be made a master of their trade at last
a better pitch on the market square than the one they have
to see the sea once before they die
to find the nerve to speak plainly to the one they are sweet on
news of a brother who went off soldiering and stopped writing
enough coin to leave this place and not come back
to be left alone by everyone for one whole day
a seat among those who run the town
to fix the roof before the rains come back
an apprentice worth teaching, which they have never had
to see a rival in the same trade brought low
a cure for a sick parent that the local healer cannot manage
the coin and the leave to make a pilgrimage
to be taken seriously by the people who give them orders
to get back something of their mother's that was stolen last winter
a quiet drink at the end of the day without anybody's troubles in it
a promotion they believe they were passed over for
a cargo that will finally make the journey pay
a boat of their own instead of shares in someone else's
one good harvest after two bad ones
someone they trust to read them a letter they have kept for a month
to be forgiven by someone they wronged years ago
a traveller with a story they have not heard before
to prove a doubter wrong in front of the whole street
a road home that the bandits do not know about
to sell the business for a fair price and rest
to be counted as one of the town's own, not an outsider
a coat that will actually keep the cold out this year
the secret of a rival's recipe
a dog of their own, which they have asked for every day this year
to be allowed to stay up for the whole of the next festival
to beat the older children in the race to the well
to be trusted with a real errand, alone

goals.text: to raise a family and see them settled
to become the best at their work anyone in the region has seen
to make one thing so fine it outlasts them
to fall properly in love, once
to rise to command the ones who command them now
to see the far side of the world with their own eyes
to have their name sung in taverns they have never visited
to be rich enough never to count coin again
a shop of their own with their name over the door
to build something the town will still use in a hundred years
to pay back the one who ruined their family
to make peace with a parent or child they stopped speaking to
to be counted among the faithful when their god calls them
a small house somewhere quiet to grow old in
to learn to read and write properly
to find what their grandfather swore he buried and never came back for
to owe nobody anything, ever again
to pass on everything they know before it is lost
to be somewhere they are wanted
to see one particular crime answered for
to live one story worth telling before settling down
to restore a family name that was disgraced
to be rid of an old hurt that aches every winter
to go back to the village they left as a child
to be a knight — or at least a guard — when they grow up
to sail away on a real ship one day
to be as good at their parent's trade as their parent is

hobbies.text: whittles small animals out of scrap wood
plays dice in the back of the tavern
sings in the tavern when the evening gets loud
watches the birds and knows every one by its call
keeps a small garden that is better tended than it needs to be
collects odd stones and keeps the best on a windowsill
plays cards for small stakes and remembers every hand
tells long stories to anybody who stays still
keeps pigeons on the roof and races them
brews a private batch of something strong
embroiders flowers onto whatever will hold still
carves game pieces and plays anyone who will sit down
walks the edge of town at dusk, the same way every night
reads old histories and argues about them
throws knives at a target behind the house
arm-wrestles for drinks and loses gracefully
collects gossip the way other people collect coins
learns songs from travellers and writes the words down wrong
paints small pictures on broken pottery
keeps bees and talks to them
knows the stars and names them by their old names
keeps a small household shrine spotless
mends other people's broken things for nothing
cooks elaborate meals for friends on rest days
goes to watch the horse fair every season
fishes off the bridge on rest days and catches nothing
dances at every festival, badly and happily
draws maps of places they have only heard about
feeds every stray cat on the street
trades riddles and keeps the good ones in their head
carves their mark into things they have built or mended
bets on anything that can be bet on
keeps a tally of the weather and is proud of it
is teaching themself the fiddle, slowly
spars with a friend behind the stables
collects foreign coins and never spends them
skims stones and counts every bounce out loud
plays at being a guard with a stick for a sword
follows interesting strangers at a distance, badly
